summary.text:
The task is to judge whether the exact BOOK ENTRY for "Sin" is the best explanation of the supplied scriptural evidence, compared to the common interpretation.
The book entry is PERSUADED. Its core identification—that sin is defined in Scripture as the transgression of the law—matches the supplied texts exactly and is the strongest reading among the alternatives. The common interpretations (A–D) correctly note that 1 John 3:4 identifies sin with lawlessness and that Romans 3:23 frames sin as falling short of God’s glory, but they treat these as one facet of a broader concept (rebellion, missing the mark, original sin, etc.). The entry isolates the explicit definitional statement in 1 John 3:4 and the two Romans verses that immediately follow it ( 4:15 and 3:20), which together state that sin is known only through the law and that transgression is the operative category. Those verses do not contradict the broader metaphors; they simply supply the narrow, self-referential definition the entry quotes.

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
